questions.question: Which group of the periodic table contains the noble gases, which are known for being highly unreactive?
options: Group 1
Group 7
Group 0
Group 2

questions.question: What physical state are all noble gases in when at room temperature?
options: Gas
Liquid
Solid
Some are liquids and some are gases

questions.question: What atomic feature makes the noble gases extremely stable and unreactive?
options: They have complete outer electron shells
They have more neutrons than protons
They have very low atomic masses
They share electrons easily with other gases

questions.question: As you move down the elements in Group 0, what happens to their density and boiling points?
options: Both density and boiling points decrease
Density increases but boiling points decrease
Density decreases but boiling points increase
Both density and boiling points increase

questions.question: How do the chemical and physical properties of elements generally change as you move down a specific group in the periodic table?
options: They stay completely identical
They change gradually
They change randomly from one element to the next
They change only for the first two elements

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the physical properties and reactivity trend of Group 1 metals?
options: They are hard, dense, and become less reactive down the group
They are soft, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive down the group
They are soft, extremely dense, and become less reactive down the group
They are hard, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive down the group

questions.question: Why are Group 1 metals commonly referred to as the alkali metals?
options: They react with acids to form alkaline salts
They react with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas
They form an alkaline gas when heated in air
They are found naturally dissolved in alkaline lakes

questions.question: What are the products when a Group 2 metal reacts with a dilute acid?
options: A salt and hydrogen gas
An alkaline solution and oxygen gas
A metal halide and water
A salt and oxygen gas

questions.question: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals compare to Group 1 metals in the same period?
options: Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals
Group 2 metals are equally reactive to Group 1 metals
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals
Group 2 metals do not react, unlike Group 1 metals

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the Group 7 elements (halogens)?
options: They are all metals that form coloured liquids
They are non-metals that have coloured, mostly toxic vapours
They are highly unreactive gases that do not form compounds
They are shiny, soft solids with very high melting points

questions.question: How does the physical state of Group 7 elements at room temperature change as you go down the group?
options: From solid to gas
From liquid to gas
From gas to solid
From solid to liquid

questions.question: What is the trend in reactivity as you move down Group 7 of the periodic table?
options: Reactivity increases
Reactivity decreases
Reactivity stays exactly the same
Reactivity decreases then suddenly increases

questions.question: What substance is produced when a halogen reacts with a Group 1 or Group 2 metal?
options: A metal hydroxide
A metal oxide
A metal halide
An acidic solution

questions.question: Which of the following statements about metal halides is correct?
options: They are completely insoluble in water
They are soluble in water
They only dissolve in dilute acids
They form insoluble gaseous precipitates in water

questions.question: In the periodic table, what are the vertical columns and horizontal rows called?
options: Columns are called periods, and rows are called groups
Columns are called groups, and rows are called periods
Columns are called families, and rows are called categories
Columns are called series, and rows are called tables

questions.question: Who was the Russian scientist responsible for developing the periodic table?
options: Dimitri Mendeleev
John Dalton
Marie Curie
Ernest Rutherford

questions.question: How are elements organised in the periodic table?
options: In alphabetical order by their chemical names
Into groups and periods based on their properties
By their discovery date from oldest to newest
In order of their abundance in the Earth's crust

questions.question: What can be said about elements that are located in the same group of the periodic table?
options: They have similar properties
They have identical boiling points
They have the same atomic mass
They are all in the same physical state at room temperature
